$janet.$comment: Not JSON Schema. Read by scripts/Test-OutputContracts.ps1.
$janet.$comment.oneShape: Both tools answer with this one shape. server_rotate answers state 'started' the moment the detached launcher is running; server_rotation reads the same files back later, after the server answering may itself have been replaced.
$janet.$comment.namesOnly: servingEnvironment carries variable NAMES and never values: a launcher's environment can hold secrets, and this envelope is served to callers and written into transcripts.

contract.description: Bumped only by a format change.

server.description: Which server this rotation is of.

state.description: never: no rotation is recorded. started: launched by this very call. running: the launcher is still alive and has written no result. succeeded / failed: the launcher wrote its result. unknown: the launcher is gone and left no result -- killed, or the machine restarted -- so the outcome cannot be told from here; 'currentBuild' and the log are the evidence left.

startedAt.description: When the launcher was started, UTC. Null only when state is never.

finishedAt.description: When the rotation script finished or threw, UTC. Null while it runs, and when it never reported.

launcherPid.description: The detached pwsh running the rotation. Not the new server's pid: the script starts that, and its own log names it.

error.description: What the rotation script threw, verbatim -- a failed publish names the locked file; a server that died on start names its log. Null unless state is failed.

currentBuild.description: The build directory the 'current' junction resolves to right now, which is what a restarted server runs from. Null when there is no junction yet.

logPath.description: The rotation script's full output, kept after the call.

logTail.description: The last non-blank lines of that log (at most 15), so a failure arrives with its context. Empty when there is no log.

target.description: Exactly what Update-McpServer.ps1 is given for this server.

root.description: Directory holding the build-* directories and the 'current' junction.

processName.description: The process stopped and restarted. Only HTTP servers running from under root are stopped; stdio servers belong to their clients and are left alone.

serverArguments.description: Arguments the new server starts with.

toolProjects.description: Global tools packed and reinstalled in the same pass (the janet CLI). Empty for razorgraph.

port.description: From .mcp.json. Passed as --port so the script waits for the new server to LISTEN; null when .mcp.json declares none, and then the script does not wait.

servingEnvironment.description: What the server answering THIS call did to its own launcher's environment at startup. Null when it did not run the normalisation at all (an older build).

applied.description: False when the inherited environment was kept -- see skippedBecause.

skippedBecause.description: Why it was kept: JANET_KEEP_ENVIRONMENT set, or not Windows. Null when applied.

dropped.description: Variables the launcher had and the clean environment does not -- the leaks, e.g. Platform from a Visual Studio prompt.

changed.description: Variables whose value differed, typically PATH.
